title: lichen_rollcall_status_to_cbor: unguarded STATUS_STRINGS index, OOB on caller-supplied enum
description: checkin.c:1262 indexes STATUS_STRINGS[t->status] (3-element) with status copied verbatim from caller via public lichen_rollcall_record_responded/record_missing (checkin.c:1706-1720). Any value >=3 is OOB read/hard-fault class on MCU. Sibling lichen_checkin_to_cbor defends exactly this via status_str()==NULL -> -INVALID_STATUS (checkin.c:439-444). Fix: validate status in record_* entry points and/or guard index in status_to_cbor, symmetric with checkin codec; host-suite test with out-of-range enum.
close_reason: lichen_rollcall_status_to_cbor no longer indexes STATUS_STRINGS unguarded: responded-loop status now goes through lichen_checkin_status_str() with a NULL -> -LICHEN_CHECKIN_ERR_INVALID_STATUS fail-closed return, symmetric with lichen_checkin_to_cbor's defense. lichen_rollcall_record_responded/record_missing validate track->status at the public entry points (status is rendered when a track moves back to responded), so stored state can never hold an out-of-range value. Header docs updated with the new return values. Regression test_rollcall_invalid_status_rejected added: bogus enum 99 rejected by both record_* entry points with lists untouched, encoder returns -INVALID_STATUS on a hostile struct, valid status still renders and round-trips. Evidence: host suite 16/16 pass under ASan/UBSan; cppcheck findings identical to baseline (5 pre-existing in main.c, none new).
